A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HiPPO Zoo work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison. Retained material can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments on nonlinear system identification, selective copying, associative recall, variable-horizon reconstruction, and forecasting in Sections 3.1–3.5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds synthetic-task baseline and scaling results, WikiText-2 language-modeling results, and analysis of learned Salience and Mamba timestep signals.

M1.justification: The five extension procedures remain intact, but Appendix B corrects the specified base models: the Leg-T diagonal changes from +b_n b_k to -b_n b_k, and the Leg-S basis changes from L_n(exp(-tau)) to L_n(1-exp(-tau)). These are limited model-specification corrections; the PDFs do not establish corresponding implementation changes.

E1.justification: v2 adds character-level language modeling on WikiText-2-raw in Section 3.6 and Appendix F, extending evaluation from synthetic mechanism demonstrations to natural-language data. The original synthetic task coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The selective-copying and associative-recall comparisons now include vanilla HiPPO, HiPPO with an MLP, LSTM, S4D, and Transformer configurations (Table 1). Language modeling adds evaluated LSTM, S4D, and Mamba comparisons (Table 4). Figure 4 also adds an Oracle Error reference curve absent from the corresponding v1 experiment.

E3.justification: New Appendix C.6 specifies 3,500 sequences with 70/15/15 splits, 4,000 optimization steps, validation-selected learning rates, parameter matching, and nearest-token accuracy. Follow-up experiments vary depth, positional embeddings, capacity, data, and optimization budgets. Appendix F introduces official language-modeling splits, perplexity evaluation, and validation-based early stopping. These are added evaluation designs, rather than established changes to the original illustrative experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds associative-recall scaling and positional-embedding investigations (Table 3), a kernel/address-spacing diagnostic examining memory interference (Figure 6), and PCA/regression analysis comparing Salience and Mamba timestep signals (Appendix F.3). The original multiscale-variant analysis remains, with its figure renumbered from 6 to 7.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 1A first reports Volterra learning curves as mean ± SEM across five independent runs; v1 provides neither this run count nor that uncertainty statement. This establishes new reporting, not an increase from a known earlier run count. Reconstruction experiments retain their existing 64-trajectory SEM reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 1 reports 100.0% selective-copying accuracy for Salience HiPPO and 100.0% associative-recall accuracy for Associative Memory HiPPO. Table 3 adds scaling outcomes, including 99.7% recall for a two-layer Transformer with positional embeddings and doubled steps. Table 4 reports language-modeling perplexities of 6.80 for HiPPO+MLP, 7.52 for Salience, and 20.41 for Associative Memory, versus 5.54 for single-layer Mamba. Appendix F.3 adds 79% first-PC variance and regression R² values of 0.38 and 0.01. These are newly reported results, not cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 explicitly transforms the input using f(phi^-1(t1)) and corrects the real-time history weighting to omega_1(phi(T)-phi(s))g(s), accounting for lag from the current time. Appendix B also corrects the Leg-T diagonal and Leg-S basis argument. The principal multiscale and forecasting derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstracts, introductions, and closing synthesis retain the same central contribution: five explicit polynomial-memory extensions realizing selected SSM capabilities while preserving interpretability and online updates. The additional evaluations do not redefine that core contribution.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands applicability and mechanism discussion: it interprets language-modeling failures, examines why baseline architectures succeed or fail on recall, and discusses computational tradeoffs. Appendix F.3 explicitly acknowledges that Salience–Mamba differences cannot isolate scalar versus vector adaptivity without further ablations. Appendix F.2 also introduces the stronger, insufficiently established interpretation that continuous addressing is fundamentally mismatched to language prediction.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a code-access link absent from v1 and adds replication information for the baseline, scaling, and language-modeling experiments. Details include optimizer weight decay, learning-rate selection, early stopping, SSM timestep ranges, and Mamba timestep dimensionality. The original experiment descriptions largely remain intact.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Hochreiter and Schmidhuber for LSTM, Vaswani et al. for Transformers, and Merity et al. for WikiText-2. The existing HiPPO/SSM literature discussion and positioning around explicit, interpretable memory remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are retained. v2 makes local language and terminology edits, expands the history-measure explanation, adds the new evaluation sections, and replaces the short Conclusion with a Discussion organized around performance, computational tradeoffs, and practitioner guidance.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual evidence with three new results tables and an associative-memory kernel heatmap. Figure 1 reverses panel order and adds uncertainty bands; Figure 4 adds an oracle curve and legend. Several retained figures move between columns or pages. The original systems table and multiscale appendix plot remain as Table 2 and Figure 7.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical grounding: baseline and scaling comparisons address gaps in v1's synthetic demonstrations, while WikiText-2 exposes important transfer limitations. Corrected mathematical specifications, added uncertainty reporting, and a code-access link also improve assessability and reproducibility. These gains outweigh localized weaknesses, including Figure 6's 16-versus-32 coefficient discrepancy and claims of fundamental architectural mismatch that exceed the tested settings.
